newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajik foes to talk in Moscow, no preconditions.
newsitem.headline: Tajik foes to talk in Moscow, no preconditions.

text.p: The two leaders of the warring sides in Tajikistan's bitter four-year civil war agreed on Tuesday to hold further talks without preconditions in Moscow next week, Russia's Interfax news agency said.
Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov met Islamist opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri in northern Afghanistan to lay the groundwork for a peace agreement to be signed in Moscow.
Interfax gave no further details. But an aide to Nuri cited earlier by the agency said a ceasefire accord and some form of coalition government were under consideration.
The meeting is scheduled to take place on December 19.
Fighting has flared in the former Soviet republic since the peace talks were announced at the end of last month, with each side trying to beef up its position at the negotiating table.
The four-year civil war has left tens of thousands dead and many more homeless in the remote, mountainous country bordering Afghanistan and China.
